method: membrane-kv-runtime-relocate-probe 'cycle' mode with 'invalidate' flag set -- every cycle: llama_synchronize -> relocate_layer(retain=false, i.e. real free attempted) -> llama_invalidate_graph_cache -> decode. Both directions exercised every cycle (toggles CPU<->GPU). ctx=8192 (large enough for the per-cycle VRAM delta to be clearly visible above nvidia-smi's 1 MiB measurement granularity).
no_vram_creep: confirmed -- VRAM oscillates cleanly between the two placements' expected values every cycle, no monotonic drift across 50 cycles
no_rss_creep: confirmed -- RSS growth over 50 cycles is a few KB (well within allocator/process bookkeeping noise), not a leak trend
poison_tests_still_prove_latest_backing_: Not re-run per-cycle in this mode (retain=false means old backing is genuinely freed each cycle, so there is nothing left to poison by design -- poisoning would itself be a use-after-free). The authoritative-backing claim for THIS exact fixed configuration was instead proven once, directly, via repro2's ground-truth poison test with retain_old_backing_for_research=true + invalidate_cache=true (see minimal_repro.json / results/phase12/runtime-relocate/repeated_same_layer_retained.json's methodology, reused here): decode output after 2 relocations matches an independent clean reference exactly, and the diagnostic tensor/buffer capture correctly shows the NEW placement (unlike the pre-fix run), confirming the graph is genuinely rebuilt and reading the current backing.
